bindings.caption: Dissolve procedural CdBr2 and MPA in deionized water. CdCl2·2.5H2O materials list versus CdBr2 procedural precursor. Two named identities with explicit uncertainty; recipe follows reported procedural CdBr2 without claiming conflict resolved. (main p2 §2.1 versus p3 §2.3/p4 §3.1) Generic apparatus cue; vessel dimensions, quantitative liquid level and spatial layout are not measured source geometry.

Adjust solution to pH 10.9. The precise value belongs to method prose. Figure 1a separately labels pH 10–12. Generic apparatus cue; vessel dimensions, quantitative liquid level and spatial layout are not measured source geometry.

Transfer to a three-necked flask and reflux under N2. No flask capacity, ramp rate, heating bath or pre-injection hold is specified. Figure 1a reports a 3 h reflux duration and pH10–12; these are tied to their figure locator. Method pH10.9 is retained at the adjustment step. Exact duration placement relative to dropwise injection is unresolved; no additional post-injection dwell is created. Generic apparatus cue; vessel dimensions, quantitative liquid level and spatial layout are not measured source geometry.

Inject NaHTe dropwise into the refluxing mixture. Reported Cd:MPA:Te=1.51:1:2.70. No feed-amount reconstruction from this ratio and no assumption that the full NaHTe preparation was injected. Generic apparatus cue; vessel dimensions, quantitative liquid level and spatial layout are not measured source geometry.

Purify by ultracentrifugation. No duration, wash sequence, rotor radius, retained fraction or redispersion volume is stated.
